name: Elliptic flow of unitary gases and the QGP
summary: Strongly interacting Fermi gases released from anisotropic traps expand elliptically like the QGP's elliptic flow; both are nearly perfect fluids with eta/s near hbar/4 pi k_B.
breaks: Non-relativistic vs relativistic hydrodynamics; scales differ by ~1e19 in temperature; the QGP has gauge degrees of freedom and a crossover, the gas has none.
sources: O'Hara et al. (2002). "Observation of a Strongly Interacting Degenerate Fermi Gas of Atoms". *Science* 298, 2179. [arXiv:cond-mat/0212463](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0212463)
Schäfer & Teaney (2009). "Nearly perfect fluidity: from cold atomic gases to hot quark gluon plasmas". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 72, 126001. [arXiv:0904.3107](https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.3107)
Cao et al. (2011). "Universal Quantum Viscosity in a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 331, 58. [arXiv:1007.2625](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.2625)

name: Cold-atom analogues of colour superfluidity
summary: Three-component Fermi gases with attractive interactions can form colour-superfluid and trion ('baryon') phases, an analogue of colour superconductivity and confinement in the dense QCD phase diagram.
breaks: No gauge field or gluon dynamics; trion formation is not confinement; densities map only qualitatively.

name: Unitary Fermi gas and dilute neutron matter
summary: The neutron-neutron scattering length (-18.5 fm) far exceeds the effective range, so low-density neutron matter is close to the unitary Fermi gas realized at Feshbach resonances; the measured Bertsch parameter benchmarks neutron-star crust EOS calculations.
sources: Carlson, Chang, Pandharipande & Schmidt (2003). "Superfluid Fermi Gases with Large Scattering Length". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 91, 050401. [arXiv:physics/0303094](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0303094)
Ku et al. (2012). "Revealing the Superfluid Lambda Transition in the Universal Thermodynamics of a Unitary Fermi Gas". *Science* 335, 563. [arXiv:1110.3309](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.3309)

name: Hoyle state as an alpha-particle condensate
summary: The 7.65 MeV Hoyle state of carbon-12 that enables triple-alpha burning has been described as a dilute gas of alpha clusters occupying one orbital, a nuclear analogue of a Bose condensate.
breaks: Only three or four bosons with Pauli effects among constituent nucleons; the condensate fraction is model dependent and debated.
sources: Tohsaki, Horiuchi, Schuck & Röpke (2001). "Alpha Cluster Condensation in 12C and 16O". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 87, 192501. [arXiv:nucl-th/0110014](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0110014)

name: Feshbach resonances: from nuclear reactions to cold atoms
summary: Feshbach developed closed-channel resonance theory for nuclear reactions; the same coupled-channel physics, tuned by magnetic field, became the main tool for controlling interactions in ultracold gases.
sources: Feshbach (1958). "Unified theory of nuclear reactions". *Ann. Phys.* 5, 357. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1)
Chin et al. (2010). "Feshbach resonances in ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1225. [arXiv:0812.1496](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1496)

name: BCS pairing in nuclei and Fermi gases
summary: Odd-even mass staggering and moments of inertia reflect BCS-like pairing in finite nuclei, the same gap equation as in BEC-BCS-crossover Fermi gases, with the cold-atom crossover a tunable laboratory for the regime. See the pairing-across-scales theme.
sources: Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [arXiv:nucl-th/0210033](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0210033)

name: Scissors modes in deformed nuclei and BECs
summary: The scissors mode, a counter-rotation of proton and neutron clouds discovered in deformed nuclei, was predicted and observed in anisotropic BECs as a signature of superfluid irrotational flow.
breaks: In nuclei the mode is a proton-neutron relative rotation in a finite fermion system; in a BEC it is the tilt oscillation of a single bosonic superfluid.
sources: Guéry-Odelin & Stringari (1999). "Scissors Mode and Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 4452. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4452)

Maragò et al. (2000). "Observation of the Scissors Mode and Evidence for Superfluidity of a Trapped Bose-Einstein Condensed Gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 84, 2056. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.2056)

name: Laser-trapped radioactive atoms for weak-interaction tests
summary: Magneto-optical and dipole traps hold short-lived radioactive atoms nearly at rest, so recoiling nuclei and beta-neutrino angular correlations can be measured cleanly to search for scalar and tensor weak currents.

name: Quarkonium in the QGP as an open quantum system
summary: Heavy quark-antiquark pairs coupled to the QGP bath obey Lindblad equations derived from pNRQCD, describing screening, dissociation and regeneration of quarkonia beyond rate equations.
sources: Brambilla, Escobedo, Soto & Vairo (2017). "Quarkonium suppression in heavy-ion collisions: an open quantum system approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 96, 034021. [arXiv:1612.07248](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07248)

name: Random-matrix theory began with nuclear resonances
summary: Wigner and Dyson introduced random matrices to model neutron-resonance spacings in heavy nuclei; the nuclear data ensemble later anchored the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit link between classical chaos and Wigner-Dyson statistics.
sources: Wigner (1955). "Characteristic Vectors of Bordered Matrices With Infinite Dimensions". *Ann. Math.* 62, 548. [doi:10.2307/1970079](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970079)
Dyson (1962). "Statistical Theory of the Energy Levels of Complex Systems. I". *J. Math. Phys.* 3, 140. [doi:10.1063/1.1703773](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1703773)

Bohigas, Giannoni & Schmit (1984). "Characterization of Chaotic Quantum Spectra and Universality of Level Fluctuation Laws". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 1. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1)

name: Thermalization of an isolated QCD system
summary: Heavy-ion collisions pose the isolated-system thermalization problem at strong coupling: how a far-from-equilibrium gluon state reaches hydrodynamic behaviour in ~1 fm/c, with links to prethermalization and non-thermal fixed points studied in cold atoms.
sources: Berges, Heller, Mazeliauskas & Venugopalan (2021). "QCD thermalization: Ab initio approaches and interdisciplinary connections". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 93, 035003. [arXiv:2005.12299](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12299)

name: Compound nucleus as a thermalizing system
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus forgets how it was formed and decays statistically, an early instance of an isolated many-body quantum system thermalizing; Hauser-Feshbach and evaporation theory use nuclear temperature.
sources: Bohr (1936). "Neutron Capture and Nuclear Constitution". *Nature* 137, 344. [doi:10.1038/137344a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/137344a0)

name: Entanglement entropy in deep inelastic scattering
summary: The parton distribution probed at small x has been interpreted as the entanglement entropy between the probed region and the rest of the proton, linking DIS multiplicities to quantum information.
sources: Kharzeev & Levin (2017). "Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 114008. [arXiv:1702.03489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03489)

name: Quantum computing of nuclear ground states
summary: Variational quantum eigensolvers computed the deuteron binding energy from pionless/chiral EFT Hamiltonians on cloud processors, a first step toward quantum simulation of nuclear many-body problems.
sources: Dumitrescu et al. (2018). "Cloud Quantum Computing of an Atomic Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 210501. [arXiv:1801.03897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.03897)

name: Odd-even pairing effects in nuclei and SC islands
summary: Small superconducting islands show an even-odd ground-state energy difference from an unpaired quasiparticle, the same blocking effect behind nuclear odd-even mass staggering; quasiparticle poisoning of charge qubits is its device consequence.
map: \Delta E_{\rm odd-even}\approx\Delta\ (\text{gap});\ E_{\rm odd}-E_{\rm even}=\Delta-k_BT\ln N_{\rm eff}

name: Penning-trap mass spectrometry
summary: Ion-trap techniques measure masses of exotic nuclei to 1e-8 or better via cyclotron frequencies, fixing separation energies, shell gaps and drip lines.
sources: Blaum (2006). "High-accuracy mass spectrometry with stored ions". *Phys. Rep.* 425, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.011)

name: Spin-orbit coupling and magic numbers
summary: A strong nuclear spin-orbit term splits j=l+-1/2 levels and reproduces the magic numbers; jj-coupling, Clebsch-Gordan and Wigner-Eckart machinery from atomic physics then organizes shell-model states.
breaks: Same operator algebra but different physics: nuclear spin-orbit is a strong-interaction effect, ~20x larger relative to level spacing, with inverted ordering relative to atomic fine structure.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: WKB tunnelling and the Gamow peak
summary: Thermonuclear fusion proceeds by WKB tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the product of Maxwell-Boltzmann tail and penetrability gives the Gamow peak that sets stellar and fusion-reactor rates.

name: Alpha decay as Coulomb-barrier tunnelling
summary: Gamow and Gurney-Condon explained alpha decay as tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier; the barrier-penetration factor gives the Geiger-Nuttall law spanning 20+ orders of magnitude in half-life.
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
Gurney & Condon (1928). "Wave Mechanics and Radioactive Disintegration". *Nature* 122, 439. [doi:10.1038/122439a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/122439a0)

name: Least-action paths for spontaneous fission
summary: Spontaneous-fission lifetimes are computed as imaginary-time tunnelling along least-action paths in a multidimensional collective space, an instanton/WKB calculation with a coordinate-dependent inertia.
sources: Schunck & Robledo (2016). "Microscopic theory of nuclear fission: a review". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 79, 116301. [arXiv:1511.07517](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07517)

name: Coulomb wavefunctions and the Gamow factor
summary: Charged-particle reaction rates factor into a smooth astrophysical S-factor and the Sommerfeld/Gamow penetrability that comes from exact Coulomb scattering wavefunctions at the origin.

name: Partial waves, resonances and the optical model
summary: Nuclear reaction theory is applied quantum scattering theory: phase shifts and partial waves, Breit-Wigner compound resonances, the complex optical potential (absorption via Im V), and R-matrix fits of cross sections.

name: Large scattering length: pionless EFT and cold atoms
summary: Pionless EFT for nucleons and the effective theory of Feshbach-tuned atoms share universal large-scattering-length physics: shallow dimers (deuteron), the three-body parameter and Efimov-like states in nuclei and halos.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

name: Photon-counting detectors shared with radiation detection
summary: Scintillation and gamma spectroscopy rely on single-photon-sensitive photodetectors (PMTs, SiPMs), while transition-edge-sensor microcalorimeters developed for quantum optics give eV resolution for gamma and X-ray lines.

name: Cold atoms as analog Hubbard simulators
summary: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Bose- and Fermi-Hubbard models with tunable U/t, giving clean, disorder-free access to Mott physics and magnetism that motivate condensed-matter questions.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)

name: From Hartree-Fock atoms to density functionals
summary: Self-consistent-field methods for atoms (Hartree-Fock, Thomas-Fermi, Slater's exchange approximation) led directly to density functional theory for solids.
sources: Slater (1951). "A Simplification of the Hartree-Fock Method". *Phys. Rev.* 81, 385. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.81.385](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.81.385)

name: Exciton and polariton condensation
summary: Excitons and exciton-polaritons are composite bosons that condense at high temperature because of their light mass; interlayer TMD excitons are candidate equilibrium exciton condensates.
sources: Kasprzak et al. (2006). "Bose–Einstein condensation of exciton polaritons". *Nature* 443, 409. [doi:10.1038/nature05131](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05131)

name: Synthetic spin-orbit coupling in quantum gases
summary: Raman dressing gives atoms Rashba/Dresselhaus-like spin-orbit coupling, emulating spintronic Hamiltonians in clean, tunable neutral gases.
breaks: Neutral atoms carry no charge current; synthetic SOC comes with heating from spontaneous emission.
sources: Lin, Jiménez-García & Spielman (2011). "Spin–orbit-coupled Bose–Einstein condensates". *Nature* 471, 83. [arXiv:1103.3522](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3522)

name: BEC-BCS crossover connects pairs and condensates
summary: Feshbach-tuned Fermi gases cross continuously from BCS Cooper pairing to a BEC of tightly bound molecules; the same gap and number equations describe superconductors at weak coupling.
sources: Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)
Regal, Greiner & Jin (2004). "Observation of Resonance Condensation of Fermionic Atom Pairs". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 92, 040403. [arXiv:cond-mat/0401554](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0401554)

name: Preformed pairs and the BEC-BCS crossover
summary: Short coherence lengths in cuprates place them between BCS and BEC limits; the pseudogap has been compared to preformed pairs above T_c in the cold-atom crossover.
breaks: Cuprate pairing is d-wave in a doped Mott insulator with competing orders; the cold-atom crossover is s-wave in a clean continuum gas.
sources: Randeria & Taylor (2014). "Crossover from Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer to Bose-Einstein Condensation and the Unitary Fermi Gas". *Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 5, 209. [arXiv:1306.5785](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5785)

name: Bloch bands in optical lattices
summary: Atoms in optical lattices obey Bloch's theorem with tight-binding bands and Wannier functions; Bloch oscillations, unobservable in solids because of scattering, are seen directly.
sources: Ben Dahan et al. (1996). "Bloch Oscillations of Atoms in an Optical Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 76, 4508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.4508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.4508)

name: Moire materials as solid-state quantum simulators
summary: Twisted bilayers realize tunable lattice models (triangular Hubbard, flat Chern bands) by twist angle and gating, playing the role optical lattices play for atoms.
breaks: Moire electrons have long-range Coulomb interactions, phonons and disorder; filling and interactions are tuned differently from cold atoms.
sources: Kennes et al. (2021). "Moiré heterostructures as a condensed-matter quantum simulator". *Nature Phys.* 17, 155. [arXiv:2011.12638](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.12638)

name: Superexchange observed with cold atoms
summary: In optical double wells, second-order tunnelling produces superexchange J=4t^2/U between spins, measured in real time.
sources: Trotzky et al. (2008). "Time-Resolved Observation and Control of Superexchange Interactions with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Science* 319, 295. [arXiv:0712.1853](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1853)

name: Quantum simulation of correlated-electron problems
summary: Strongly correlated electron problems (doped Hubbard, pseudogap, stripes) that resist numerics are posed to cold-atom simulators, whose measurements now benchmark DMFT, DMRG and QMC.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)

name: Superfluid-Mott transition in optical lattices
summary: Deep optical lattices map exactly onto the Bose-Hubbard model; tuning lattice depth drove the superfluid-Mott insulator quantum phase transition, and quantum gas microscopes now image Hubbard correlations site by site.
sources: Jaksch et al. (1998). "Cold Bosonic Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 81, 3108. [arXiv:cond-mat/9805329](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9805329)
Greiner et al. (2002). "Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms". *Nature* 415, 39. [doi:10.1038/415039a](https://doi.org/10.1038/415039a)

name: Fermi-Hubbard simulators target cuprate physics
summary: Quantum gas microscopes observed long-range antiferromagnetism and then hole-doped correlations in the 2D Fermi-Hubbard model, addressing the doped-Mott-insulator physics of cuprates.
sources: Mazurenko et al. (2017). "A cold-atom Fermi–Hubbard antiferromagnet". *Nature* 545, 462. [arXiv:1612.08436](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08436)

name: Chern bands and Hofstadter models with cold atoms
summary: Shaken and laser-assisted-tunnelling optical lattices realized the Haldane and Harper-Hofstadter models, measuring Chern numbers of synthetic quantum-Hall bands.
sources: Jotzu et al. (2014). "Experimental realization of the topological Haldane model with ultracold fermions". *Nature* 515, 237. [arXiv:1406.7874](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7874)
Aidelsburger et al. (2013). "Realization of the Hofstadter Hamiltonian with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 111, 185301. [arXiv:1308.0321](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0321)

name: Nuclear-spin bath decoherence of dot spins
summary: In GaAs dots the electron spin decoheres through hyperfine coupling to ~1e6 nuclear spins, a central-spin model of system-bath decoherence that drove the move to isotopically purified Si.
sources: Khaetskii, Loss & Glazman (2002). "Electron Spin Decoherence in Quantum Dots due to Interaction with Nuclei". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 88, 186802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0201303](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0201303)

name: Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in Josephson junctions
summary: Caldeira and Leggett's theory of dissipative tunnelling and the 1985 observation of quantized levels in a current-biased junction showed a macroscopic phase variable obeys quantum mechanics (Nobel 2025).
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Quantum tunnelling in a dissipative system". *Ann. Phys.* 149, 374. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(83)90202-6)

Martinis, Devoret & Clarke (1985). "Energy-Level Quantization in the Zero-Voltage State of a Current-Biased Josephson Junction". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 55, 1543. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1543](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1543)

name: Light-induced anomalous Hall effect in graphene
summary: Circularly polarized light opens a Floquet gap at graphene's Dirac points; an anomalous Hall response was measured in ultrafast transport.
sources: Oka & Aoki (2009). "Photovoltaic Hall effect in graphene". *Phys. Rev. B* 79, 081406. [arXiv:0807.4767](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.4767)
McIver et al. (2020). "Light-induced anomalous Hall effect in graphene". *Nature Phys.* 16, 38. [arXiv:1811.03522](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03522)

name: Floquet topological insulators
summary: Periodic driving (circularly polarized light) opens topological gaps in trivial bands; Floquet bands carry Chern and anomalous winding invariants beyond static classification.
sources: Kitagawa et al. (2010). "Topological characterization of periodically driven quantum systems". *Phys. Rev. B* 82, 235114. [arXiv:1010.6126](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.6126)
Lindner, Refael & Galitski (2011). "Floquet topological insulator in semiconductor quantum wells". *Nature Phys.* 7, 490. [arXiv:1008.1792](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.1792)

name: Non-Hermitian band topology
summary: Gain and loss extend band topology to point and line gaps; spectral winding gives the skin effect and modifies bulk-boundary correspondence, enlarging the tenfold classification.
sources: Gong et al. (2018). "Topological Phases of Non-Hermitian Systems". *Phys. Rev. X* 8, 031079. [arXiv:1802.07964](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07964)

name: Bulk Fermi arcs from exceptional points
summary: Finite quasiparticle lifetimes make the effective Hamiltonian non-Hermitian; Weyl or Dirac nodes split into exceptional rings joined by bulk Fermi arcs.
sources: Kozii & Fu (2024). "Non-Hermitian topological theory of finite-lifetime quasiparticles: Prediction of bulk Fermi arc due to exceptional point". [arXiv:1708.05841](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05841)

name: Random-matrix theory of quantum transport
summary: Universal conductance fluctuations and weak localization in chaotic cavities follow random-matrix statistics of transmission eigenvalues, the quantum-chaos framework applied to transport.
sources: Beenakker (1997). "Random-matrix theory of quantum transport". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 69, 731. [arXiv:cond-mat/9612179](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9612179)

name: Planckian dissipation and the chaos bound
summary: Strange metals relax at the Planckian rate hbar/tau ~ k_BT, the same scale as the quantum chaos bound; SYK-type models realize both maximal chaos and linear-in-T resistivity.
sources: Hartnoll (2015). "Theory of universal incoherent metallic transport". *Nature Phys.* 11, 54. [arXiv:1405.3651](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3651)
Li et al. (2024). "Strange Metal and Superconductor in the Two-Dimensional Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 133, 186502. [arXiv:2406.07608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07608)

name: Quantum of thermal conductance
summary: A single ballistic channel carries at most one heat quantum; mesoscopic conductors serve as quantum heat engines and refrigerators analysed with Landauer heat currents.
sources: Jezouin et al. (2013). "Quantum Limit of Heat Flow Across a Single Electronic Channel". *Science* 342, 601. [doi:10.1126/science.1241912](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1241912)

name: Topological quantum computation with anyons
summary: Braiding non-Abelian anyons of a topologically ordered phase implements gates protected by topology, turning a condensed-matter phase into a quantum computer architecture.
sources: Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)
Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)

name: Josephson junction as the nonlinear qubit element
summary: The dissipationless nonlinear inductance of a Josephson junction is what makes superconducting circuits anharmonic and hence usable as qubits.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Non-Abelian anyons in fractional quantum Hall states
summary: The nu=5/2 state is a candidate Moore-Read phase with Ising anyons; interferometry and braiding there are a proposed route to topological qubits.
sources: Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)

name: Majorana zero modes as topological qubits
summary: Majorana zero modes at Kitaev-chain ends store a qubit in nonlocal fermion parity; braiding gives protected Clifford gates. Experimental claims in nanowires remain contested.
sources: Kitaev (2001). "Unpaired Majorana fermions in quantum wires". *Phys.-Usp.* 44, 131. [arXiv:cond-mat/0010440](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0010440)
Nayak et al. (2008). "Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1083. [arXiv:0707.1889](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1889)

name: Topological entanglement entropy
summary: Topological order leaves a universal negative constant in the entanglement entropy area law, set by the total quantum dimension of the anyons.
sources: Kitaev & Preskill (2006). "Topological Entanglement Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110404. [arXiv:hep-th/0510092](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0510092)
Levin & Wen (2006). "Detecting Topological Order in a Ground State Wave Function". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110405. [arXiv:cond-mat/0510613](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0510613)

name: Area laws make DMRG and tensor networks work
summary: Gapped ground states obey entanglement area laws, so matrix-product states with bounded bond dimension represent them faithfully; DMRG is variational optimization over MPS.
sources: White (1992). "Density matrix formulation for quantum renormalization groups". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 69, 2863. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863)
Hastings (2007). "An area law for one-dimensional quantum systems". *J. Stat. Mech.* 0708, P08024. [arXiv:0705.2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.2024)

name: Donor and Si/SiGe spin qubits
summary: Silicon spin qubits rely on semiconductor physics: donor levels, valley splitting, isotopic purification of Si-28 and CMOS fabrication.
sources: Kane (1998). "A silicon-based nuclear spin quantum computer". *Nature* 393, 133. [doi:10.1038/30156](https://doi.org/10.1038/30156)

name: 2D materials as hosts for spin and valley qubits
summary: Graphene and TMD quantum dots offer weak hyperfine coupling and valley degrees of freedom as alternative qubit hosts.
sources: Trauzettel, Bulaev, Loss & Burkard (2007). "Spin qubits in graphene quantum dots". *Nature Phys.* 3, 192. [arXiv:cond-mat/0611252](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0611252)

name: NV magnetometry images electron hydrodynamics
summary: Nitrogen-vacancy centres used as nanoscale quantum magnetometers imaged the Poiseuille flow profile of the Dirac fluid in graphene.
sources: Ku et al. (2020). "Imaging viscous flow of the Dirac fluid in graphene". *Nature* 583, 537. [arXiv:1905.10791](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10791)

name: Gate-defined quantum-dot spin qubits
summary: Single electrons confined in gate-defined quantum dots carry spin qubits controlled by exchange (Loss-DiVincenzo); Coulomb blockade and charge sensing come from mesoscopic quantum-dot physics.
sources: Loss & DiVincenzo (1998). "Quantum computation with quantum dots". *Phys. Rev. A* 57, 120. [arXiv:cond-mat/9701055](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9701055)

name: Quantum algorithms for correlated materials
summary: Phase estimation, VQE and Hamiltonian simulation target ground states and dynamics of Hubbard-type models that classical numerics cannot reach, the leading candidate for quantum advantage.
sources: Bauer, Bravyi, Motta & Chan (2020). "Quantum Algorithms for Quantum Chemistry and Quantum Materials Science". *Chem. Rev.* 120, 12685. [arXiv:2001.03685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.03685)

name: Toric code is a topologically ordered phase
summary: The surface/toric code Hamiltonian is a Z2 topologically ordered phase: logical operators are anyon loops, code distance is system size, and the threshold maps to a disorder phase transition of a random-bond Ising model.
sources: Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)
Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl & Preskill (2002). "Topological quantum memory". *J. Math. Phys.* 43, 4452. [arXiv:quant-ph/0110143](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143)

name: Phonons as qubit resource and error source
summary: Qubits couple coherently to bulk and surface-acoustic phonon modes (quantum acoustodynamics), while phonon bursts from cosmic rays break Cooper pairs and cause chip-wide correlated errors.
sources: Chu et al. (2017). "Quantum acoustics with superconducting qubits". *Science* 358, 199. [arXiv:1703.00342](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00342)
McEwen et al. (2022). "Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits". *Nature Phys.* 18, 107. [arXiv:2104.05219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05219)

name: Superconductors as the material base of qubits
summary: Superconducting qubits inherit BCS physics: the gap protects against dissipation, while quasiparticles, two-level defects and surface oxides of Nb/Al/Ta set coherence.
sources: Clarke & Wilhelm (2008). "Superconducting quantum bits". *Nature* 453, 1031. [doi:10.1038/nature07128](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature07128)

name: Quasiparticles limit qubit coherence
summary: Non-equilibrium Bogoliubov quasiparticles above the BCS gap tunnel across junctions and cause relaxation and parity switching; gap engineering and phonon traps suppress them.

name: Transmon Hamiltonian from Josephson physics
summary: A capacitively shunted Josephson junction is a quantum pendulum; at E_J/E_C ~ 50 the charge dispersion is exponentially suppressed, giving the transmon qubit.
sources: Koch et al. (2007). "Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box". *Phys. Rev. A* 76, 042319. [arXiv:cond-mat/0703002](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0703002)

name: Rydberg arrays realize a Z2 spin liquid
summary: Rydberg-blockade atom arrays on a ruby lattice prepared a state with topological string order of a Z2 quantum spin liquid, a phase long sought in frustrated magnets.
sources: Semeghini et al. (2021). "Probing topological spin liquids on a programmable quantum simulator". *Science* 374, 1242. [arXiv:2104.04119](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04119)

name: Exchange from spin algebra and Pauli exclusion
summary: Heisenberg exchange arises because the Coulomb energy depends on the singlet or triplet spin state through antisymmetry; addition of spin angular momenta gives the S1.S2 form.

name: Spin angular momentum as a transport degree of freedom
summary: Spintronics transports and manipulates spin angular momentum: spin precession, spin-orbit coupling (Rashba/Dresselhaus) and spin-transfer torque are the quantum mechanics of spin applied to devices.
map: \dot{\mathbf S}=\gamma\mathbf S\times\mathbf B;\ H_R=\alpha(\boldsymbol\sigma\times\mathbf k)\cdot\hat z
sources: Žutić, Fabian & Das Sarma (2004). "Spintronics: Fundamentals and applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 76, 323. [arXiv:cond-mat/0405528](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0405528)

name: Kitaev honeycomb model and Kitaev materials
summary: Kitaev's exactly solvable honeycomb model has a Z2 spin-liquid ground state with Majorana excitations; it motivates the search in alpha-RuCl3 and iridates.
sources: Kitaev (2006). "Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 2. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506438](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506438)

name: Landau levels are harmonic-oscillator levels
summary: A charged particle in a uniform field maps onto a harmonic oscillator, giving Landau levels; filling them gives the integer quantum Hall plateaus.

name: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in mesoscopic rings
summary: Phase-coherent electrons in metal rings show conductance oscillations with flux period h/e, a direct transport measurement of the Aharonov-Bohm phase.
sources: Webb et al. (1985). "Observation of h/e Aharonov-Bohm Oscillations in Normal-Metal Rings". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 54, 2696. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696)

name: Berry phase pi of graphene's Dirac electrons
summary: Pseudospin winding gives graphene electrons a pi Berry phase, producing the half-integer quantum Hall sequence and suppressed backscattering.
sources: Zhang, Tan, Stormer & Kim (2005). "Experimental observation of the quantum Hall effect and Berry's phase in graphene". *Nature* 438, 201. [arXiv:cond-mat/0509355](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0509355)

name: Emergent electromagnetism of skyrmions
summary: Electrons adiabatically following a skyrmion texture acquire a real-space Berry phase that acts as an emergent magnetic flux of one quantum per skyrmion, giving the topological Hall effect.
sources: Nagaosa & Tokura (2013). "Topological properties and dynamics of magnetic skyrmions". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 8, 899. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2013.243](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2013.243)

name: Anyon statistics as Berry phases
summary: Exchanging two quasiparticles adiabatically gives a Berry phase; for Laughlin quasiholes it equals pi times the filling, so fractional statistics is a geometric phase.
sources: Arovas, Schrieffer & Wilczek (1984). "Fractional Statistics and the Quantum Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 53, 722. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722)

name: Geometric phases organize topological matter
summary: Berry's 1984 phase gave condensed matter a unified language for polarization, anomalous Hall effects and topological phases.
sources: Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Chern number is integrated Berry curvature
summary: The Hall conductance of a filled band equals the Brillouin-zone integral of Berry curvature (TKNN); geometric-phase concepts define all band-topological invariants.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs (1982). "Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405)
Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Weyl points as Berry-curvature monopoles
summary: Berry's degeneracy monopole is realized in crystals: Weyl nodes are sources of Berry flux with integer charge, giving Fermi arcs and the chiral anomaly.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Wan et al. (2011). "Topological semimetal and Fermi-arc surface states in the electronic structure of pyrochlore iridates". *Phys. Rev. B* 83, 205101. [arXiv:1007.0016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0016)

name: Path-integral quantum Monte Carlo
summary: Imaginary-time path integrals map quantum many-body systems onto classical polymers, sampled by Monte Carlo; bosonic exchange appears as permutation cycles (superfluid helium).
sources: Ceperley (1995). "Path integrals in the theory of condensed helium". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 67, 279. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.67.279](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.67.279)

name: Born approximation behind diffraction
summary: X-ray, electron and neutron diffraction are first-Born scattering: the cross section is the Fourier transform of the scattering density, and inelastic neutron scattering measures the dynamic structure factor.
sources: Van Hove (1954). "Correlations in Space and Time and Born Approximation Scattering in Systems of Interacting Particles". *Phys. Rev.* 95, 249. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.95.249](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.95.249)

name: Kondo effect as resonant scattering
summary: Below T_K conduction electrons scatter off the Kondo singlet with phase shift pi/2, the unitary limit; the Friedel sum rule ties the phase shift to the screened charge.

name: Cavity QED with quantum dots
summary: Single quantum dots in photonic-crystal nanocavities reach strong coupling with vacuum Rabi splitting, the solid-state realization of Jaynes-Cummings physics.
sources: Yoshie et al. (2004). "Vacuum Rabi splitting with a single quantum dot in a photonic crystal nanocavity". *Nature* 432, 200. [doi:10.1038/nature03119](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature03119)

name: Strong coupling of excitons to cavity photons
summary: Excitons in microcavities reach strong coupling, forming polaritons with vacuum Rabi splitting, the Jaynes-Cummings physics of cavity QED with a collective emitter.
sources: Kasprzak et al. (2006). "Bose–Einstein condensation of exciton polaritons". *Nature* 443, 409. [doi:10.1038/nature05131](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05131)

name: Mechanical resonators are engineered phonons
summary: Optomechanical resonators are phonon modes of nanostructures; phononic band gaps, Brillouin scattering and two-level-system damping are lattice-dynamics physics.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Electron quantum optics
summary: Single-electron sources, quantum point contacts as beam splitters and edge channels as waveguides let electronic HOM and HBT experiments mirror photon statistics; shot noise is the fermionic g2.
sources: Bocquillon et al. (2013). "Coherence and Indistinguishability of Single Electrons Emitted by Independent Sources". *Science* 339, 1054. [doi:10.1126/science.1232572](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1232572)

name: Quantum-dot single-photon sources
summary: Self-assembled semiconductor quantum dots are two-level emitters that, embedded in micropillars, give bright, pure and indistinguishable single photons.
sources: Michler et al. (2000). "A Quantum Dot Single-Photon Turnstile Device". *Science* 290, 2282. [doi:10.1126/science.290.5500.2282](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.290.5500.2282)

name: Quantum emitters in 2D semiconductors
summary: Strain- and defect-localized excitons in monolayer WSe2 act as single-photon emitters, linking 2D-material excitonics to quantum-optical sources.
sources: Srivastava et al. (2015). "Optically active quantum dots in monolayer WSe2". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 10, 491. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2015.60](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2015.60)

name: Superconducting single-photon detectors
summary: SNSPDs and transition-edge sensors use photon-induced breaking of superconductivity (hotspots, steep R(T)) to count photons with high efficiency and low jitter.
sources: Gol'tsman et al. (2001). "Picosecond superconducting single-photon optical detector". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 79, 705. [doi:10.1063/1.1388868](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1388868)

name: Atom interferometry constrains screened dark energy
summary: Atoms in a high vacuum are unscreened test masses; interferometers near a source mass bound chameleon-type dark-energy forces.
sources: Hamilton et al. (2015). "Atom-interferometry constraints on dark energy". *Science* 349, 849. [arXiv:1502.03888](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03888)

name: Clock networks as dark-matter detectors
summary: Networks of atomic clocks and magnetometers could detect transient frequency shifts from passing topological-defect dark matter, or oscillations from ultralight fields.
sources: Derevianko & Pospelov (2014). "Hunting for topological dark matter with atomic clocks". *Nature Phys.* 10, 933. [arXiv:1311.1244](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1244)
Arvanitaki, Huang & Van Tilburg (2015). "Searching for dilaton dark matter with atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 91, 015015. [arXiv:1405.2925](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2925)

name: Astrocombs calibrate radial-velocity planet searches
summary: Optical frequency combs, developed for clock metrology, give spectrographs absolute, evenly spaced calibration lines for cm/s radial-velocity precision needed for Earth analogues.
sources: Steinmetz et al. (2008). "Laser Frequency Combs for Astronomical Observations". *Science* 321, 1335. [doi:10.1126/science.1161030](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1161030)
Udem, Holzwarth & Hänsch (2002). "Optical frequency metrology". *Nature* 416, 233. [doi:10.1038/416233a](https://doi.org/10.1038/416233a)

name: Quasar absorption tests of varying alpha
summary: Relative wavelengths of metal absorption lines in quasar spectra, with laboratory sensitivity coefficients, constrain cosmic variation of the fine-structure constant; reported variations remain contested.
sources: Webb et al. (1999). "Search for Time Variation of the Fine Structure Constant". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 82, 884. [arXiv:astro-ph/9803165](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9803165)

name: Hydrogen atomic physics sets recombination
summary: Recombination is delayed beyond Saha equilibrium because Lyman-alpha photons are trapped; the 2s-1s two-photon decay and Lyman-alpha redshifting control the last-scattering surface and thus the CMB acoustic scale.
sources: Peebles (1968). "Recombination of the Primeval Plasma". *Astrophys. J.* 153, 1. [doi:10.1086/149628](https://doi.org/10.1086/149628)

name: 21-cm rotation curves trace dark halos
summary: Neutral-hydrogen 21-cm emission extends rotation curves far beyond stellar disks, where flat curves give the cleanest galactic evidence for dark matter.

name: Highly charged ion spectroscopy of cluster gas
summary: X-ray lines of He- and H-like iron give temperature, abundance and turbulent velocity of intracluster gas; Hitomi's resolved Fe XXV lines measured low turbulence in Perseus.
sources: Hitomi Collaboration (2016). "The quiescent intracluster medium in the core of the Perseus cluster". *Nature* 535, 117. [arXiv:1607.04487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04487)

name: 21-cm hyperfine line and Lyman-alpha probe reionization
summary: The hydrogen hyperfine transition, its spin temperature set by collisions and Lyman-alpha pumping (Wouthuysen-Field), maps neutral gas at cosmic dawn; Gunn-Peterson Lyman-alpha absorption marks the end of reionization.
sources: Furlanetto, Oh & Briggs (2006). "Cosmology at low frequencies: The 21 cm transition and the high-redshift Universe". *Phys. Rep.* 433, 181. [arXiv:astro-ph/0608032](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0608032)
Gunn & Peterson (1965). "On the Density of Neutral Hydrogen in Intergalactic Space". *Astrophys. J.* 142, 1633. [doi:10.1086/148444](https://doi.org/10.1086/148444)

name: Lanthanide atomic data for kilonova spectra
summary: Kilonova light curves and spectra depend on the dense line forests of lanthanides and on identified features such as Sr II, requiring atomic-structure calculations of open f-shell ions.
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [arXiv:1710.05463](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05463)
Watson et al. (2019). "Identification of strontium in the merger of two neutron stars". *Nature* 574, 497. [arXiv:1910.10510](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10510)

name: Line lists for exoplanet atmosphere spectra
summary: Interpreting transmission and emission spectra needs ro-vibrational line lists of H2O, CH4, CO2 and metal atoms computed from molecular quantum mechanics.
sources: Tennyson & Yurchenko (2012). "ExoMol: molecular line lists for exoplanet and other atmospheres". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 425, 21. [arXiv:1204.0124](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0124)

name: Atomic opacities and the solar abundance problem
summary: Stellar interiors depend on computed atomic opacities; measured iron opacity at solar-interior conditions exceeds theory, a candidate resolution of the mismatch between helioseismology and low solar metal abundances.
sources: Bailey et al. (2015). "A higher-than-predicted measurement of iron opacity at solar interior temperatures". *Nature* 517, 56. [doi:10.1038/nature14048](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14048)

name: Fuzzy dark matter as a cosmic matter wave
summary: Ultralight bosonic dark matter obeys the Schrodinger-Poisson system, a Gross-Pitaevskii equation with self-gravity; galaxy halos develop solitonic cores and granular interference like condensates.
breaks: Interaction is long-range self-gravity rather than contact scattering; occupation is classical and not reached by thermal condensation; no trap or superfluid flow measurement.
sources: Hu, Barkana & Gruzinov (2000). "Fuzzy Cold Dark Matter: The Wave Properties of Ultralight Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 85, 1158. [arXiv:astro-ph/0003365](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0003365)
Schive, Chiueh & Broadhurst (2014). "Cosmic structure as the quantum interference of a coherent dark wave". *Nature Phys.* 10, 496. [arXiv:1406.6586](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.6586)

name: Fermi pressure from trapped atoms to white dwarfs
summary: Degeneracy pressure measured in trapped Fermi gases is the same Pauli effect that supports white dwarfs and neutron stars against gravity.
sources: Truscott et al. (2001). "Observation of Fermi Pressure in a Gas of Trapped Atoms". *Science* 291, 2570. [doi:10.1126/science.1059318](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1059318)

name: Superfluid vortices and pulsar glitches
summary: Neutron-star interiors are superfluid; rotation is carried by quantized vortices whose sudden unpinning from the crust is the leading explanation of pulsar glitches, the physics of vortex lattices in rotating BECs.
sources: Anderson & Itoh (1975). "Pulsar glitches and restlessness as a hard superfluidity phenomenon". *Nature* 256, 25. [doi:10.1038/256025a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/256025a0)

name: Cold molecular collisions and astrochemistry
summary: Interstellar chemistry at 10-100 K proceeds by barrierless ion-molecule reactions and tunnelling, the same low-temperature collision physics that cold-molecule experiments resolve state by state.
sources: Herbst & Klemperer (1973). "The Formation and Depletion of Molecules in Dense Interstellar Clouds". *Astrophys. J.* 185, 505. [doi:10.1086/152436](https://doi.org/10.1086/152436)

name: Cosmological Bell inequalities
summary: Bell-type observables built from primordial correlators could in principle reveal the quantum origin of structure, though decaying modes make realistic tests extremely hard.
sources: Maldacena (2016). "A model with cosmological Bell inequalities". *Fortsch. Phys.* 64, 10. [arXiv:1508.01082](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01082)
